title: SO2026 Songshan Lake Technology Elite Tennis Tournament (Silicon Valley)
content:
This weekend, tech leaders are heading to the tennis courts in the East Bay. Twelve teams, including teams from Google, Apple, Meta and NVIDIA, as well as alumni teams from Tsinghua, Peking University and other schools, are taking over the venue.

A guest lineup packed with technology talent

The event again includes an individual guest competition, led by Dr. Huican Zhu and Dr. Rongxiang Hu. Sixteen players will compete over three rounds of doubles.

Dr. Huican Zhu is a managing partner at Amino Capital and the founder of the Songshan Lake Technology Elite Tennis Tournament. His background spans image and video AI, search, cloud computing and distributed technologies. Dr. Rongxiang Hu (John Hu) combines technology and investment experience: he is a senior technology department director at NVIDIA and a founding partner of gtVision Ventures, a University of Science and Technology of China alumnus, and a PhD graduate of Auburn University. Professionals working across AI, chips and venture capital will connect through tennis.

Strong tennis, too

Players including Stanford's Connie Ma will attend. Photographer Lijian Zhang is also flying in from France to photograph the event. Around 5 p.m. on Saturday, Connie Ma and fellow players will play an exhibition match, followed by autographs and photos with spectators. Bay Area tennis fans who cannot travel to New York for the US Open can watch high-level tennis close to home.

On Saturday, the team competition begins with round-robin play in four groups. On Sunday, teams advance by placement into the Diamond, Gold and Silver divisions for semifinals and finals. The Diamond division final, around 2 p.m. on Sunday, is another match to watch.

Team rosters and scores are available on the UTR website. Detailed groups and schedules appear in the original images.
